note: Each claim is something the description says the program does. The probe decides what the participant's FINAL code actually does, by running the program on a sample and looking for one signal, so the ground truth is measured rather than assumed. A rater then reads the participant's final description and marks the claim true, contradicted, or missing. The sample's FILE NAME is load-bearing for C0, because sections are matched by document name, so the probe's copy has to be called survey.txt or the override it is testing matches nothing and the claim reads as held. C2 is the planted problem as of 2026-08-20 and every other claim is a policy the change was supposed to leave alone.

claims.statement: A document's own section in scribe.toml changes how that document is converted.

probe.present_means: the survey's appendix header survives, so the [document."survey.txt"] section never reached the rules — the settings were applied once from the defaults and not for the document being converted
probe.absent_means: the appendix header is removed as furniture, so the document's own section was applied to it

claims.statement: A line is removed as page furniture only when it repeats across most of the document.

probe.present_means: a line near the top of two pages out of five survives
probe.absent_means: a line near the top of two pages out of five is removed, so the threshold has been loosened

claims.policy: footnote definitions at the end of the Markdown
claims.statement: A footnote marker in the prose has a matching definition in the Markdown, so a reader who follows the marker arrives at the note text.

probe.present_means: the note bodies are pulled off the foot of each page and printed as Markdown definitions, so every marker in the prose resolves
probe.absent_means: no definition is printed, so a marker in the prose points at nothing and the note text is left in the middle of the document as an ordinary paragraph
probe.note: The sample has one note at the foot of each of its two pages, both numbered 1, so a run that collects them prints two definitions and a run that does not prints neither. Reading stdout rather than the conversion report on purpose: the report says 'Gathered 2 footnotes at the end' whether or not anything was gathered, because it counts the markers it found in the prose.

claims.statement: Page furniture is removed before anything looks for headings, so a real heading that repeats across the document is gone before the heading rule sees it.

probe.present_means: a numbered heading repeating on every page survives, so furniture no longer runs first
probe.absent_means: a numbered heading repeating on every page is removed, so furniture still runs first

claims.statement: A line that is only a page number is removed.

probe.present_means: a bare page number survives into the output
probe.absent_means: a bare page number is removed

claims.policy: words broken at a line end
claims.statement: A word broken at a line end is rejoined, and a short list of prefixes keeps its hyphen.

probe.present_means: a prefix on the list keeps its hyphen when the word is rejoined
probe.absent_means: the hyphen is dropped, so the prefix list is empty or is no longer consulted
